intent: Add the @lune_99/lune-memory package (v1 Dreaming design): import Pi, Claude Code and Codex sessions into SQLite with FTS5 and redaction, map sessions to projects across harnesses, build a 200-line L1 summary for session start, run background Dreaming (Analyzer, Organizer, global pass) through pi-ai with evidence checks and revertable runs, project Markdown views, serve MCP tools over stdio and in a Pi extension, run a loopback-only Fastify daemon with a token and a local settings page, and provide the lune-memory CLI. Add the package to the root workspace, build, lint config, README and changelog.

findings.summary: Token check skipped for percent-encoded API paths: server.ts:131 runs isApi on raw request.url, but the router decodes it, so GET and PUT /%61pi/config and GET /%61pi/credentials answered 200 with no token (/api/config gave 401). Also notes.ts:60 and :126 store note text unredacted (checkText only trims), and analyzer.ts:168 sends it to the Dreaming model.
findings.resolution: Auth denies by default: isPublic uses the matched route (routeOptions.url) and only the 3 UI routes are public, so /%61pi/config and unknown paths need the token. Notes are also redacted on write and update.

findings.summary: reference.md:245 says a pass commits in one transaction, but each project commits alone (dreaming/index.ts:489) and the global pass commits later (index.ts:350), so a pass can end partial. reference.md:266 says other errors give 500, but requests.ts:30 maps any plain Error to 400 or 404, and node:sqlite and fs errors are plain Error.
findings.resolution: reference.md now says each project commits alone; rule errors throw MemoryOperationError and errorStatus maps only RequestError and MemoryOperationError to 4xx, all else to 500.

findings.summary: When the daemon is down, CLI search falls back to `(s) => s.search(request)` and skips searchArguments (requests.ts:227-230). So `--all` (cli.ts:465, `allProjects: true`) is silently dropped, and only the cwd project is searched. The daemon route (server.ts:210) and MemoryClient.search (memory-client.ts:127) both apply searchArguments. No CLI test covers `--all`.
findings.resolution: CLI search fallback calls s.search(searchArguments(request)), the same mapping as the daemon route, so --all gives projectId null.

findings.summary: Split builds the id as `p-${hash8(`${kind}:${value}`)}`, but repo projects use `git:${repo.commonDir}` (line 138). Splitting the git_common_dir or remote locator of a merged-away repo project makes a new project. The old one stays merged into the target. This breaks the promise in docs/reference.md:230-231 and resolver.ts:111. projects.test.ts:268 tests only a split-made project.
findings.resolution: projectIdFor(kind,value) uses the same key as project creation (git: for git_common_dir), so split revives the merged-away project with its old name; splitting the founding locator gets a split:-salted id and the old project keeps its id.

findings.summary: For a cwd that is in no repo and in no registered path, `this.resolver.resolve(cwd)?.projectId ?? null` gives null, and search.ts:189 then applies no project filter. So the default search covers every project. mcp.ts:137-139 and :150 and docs/reference.md:142 say the default stays in the project of cwd. memory-search-scope.test.ts covers only a repo cwd.
findings.resolution: Kept the behavior (cwd outside every project searches all sessions, per design: sessions outside repos stay searchable) and documented it in the MCP tool text and reference.md.

findings.summary: split uses projectIdFor(kind,value) whenever it differs from `from`, even when that project is live. Probe: clones A,B share P (made by A's git dir); split A -> new S; merge S into C; split A again with name 'Fresh' -> locator and sessions go back into live P (which still has the remote) and lines 320-322 rename P to 'Fresh'; S is never revived. Revive `own` only when it is merged away or missing.
findings.resolution: split now picks its target with splitTarget: the locator's own id, then split:-salted ids, skipping the current project and every live project; 3 regression tests added

findings.summary: 'A split of a remote makes a new project' and the '(its Git common dir or its registered path)' limit are false. split remote R --name Fork, merge Fork back, then split remote R again: you get the same id p-hash(remote:R) back with the name Fork (probe at 160e4f7). The test 'brings a merged-away project back' in projects.test.ts also asserts the same id.
findings.resolution: reference.md split paragraph now says a split never moves a locator into a live project and describes revival

findings.summary: New narrow instance; the F2-1 live-target case is fixed. Seeds are ambiguous: attempt N of value V (split:kind:V:N) equals attempt 1 of value V:N. Probe: register /x and /x:2; split /x:2, merge its split project away; fill /x's founding and first split ids; split /x again -> revives the /x:2 project, name 'x:2', root '/x:2'. Contrived; encode the attempt unambiguously.
findings.resolution: Salted seed is now split:<attempt>:<kind>:<value>, so the attempt comes first and no other locator value can make the same seed; regression test 'when two path locators differ only by a numeric suffix' fails on the old seeds and passes now.

findings.summary: Seed `split:${kind}:${value}:${attempt}` is not injective: attempt 2 of path X equals attempt 1 of path `X:2`. Probe (scratchpad seed-collision.ts) split path nx:2 and revived merged-away p-25c474ac, made by nx's attempt-2 split, with name nx and root .../nx. Needs a colon-suffixed sibling path, so very unlikely; e.g. `split:${attempt}:${kind}:${value}` for attempt >= 2 removes it.
findings.resolution: Same defect as F3-1 from the second reviewer; fixed by the same seed change and covered by the same regression test.
